blueprint_topic: Management of Care — discharge preparation, caregiver education, equipment teaching, and home-oxygen safety
stem: A client with chronic lung disease and the client's caregiver are preparing for discharge with prescribed home oxygen. Which teaching plan should the nurse prioritize before discharge?

options.A: Teach the client and caregiver how to follow the oxygen prescription, use and maintain the equipment, troubleshoot basic problems, and prevent fire and tripping hazards.
options.B: Review the prescribed flow setting and symptom monitoring, then defer equipment-use and maintenance teaching to the oxygen supplier after the client arrives home.
options.C: Train the caregiver to operate and maintain the oxygen equipment, while directing safety teaching primarily to the client who will be wearing the oxygen.
options.D: Emphasize smoking and open-flame precautions, while telling the client that routine equipment maintenance and troubleshooting are handled by the supplier.

rationale: A is correct. The official ATS home-oxygen guideline includes a best-practice statement that patients prescribed home oxygen and their caregivers should receive instruction and training on adherence to the oxygen prescription, use, maintenance, and troubleshooting of oxygen equipment, and oxygen-safety education. ATS specifically identifies fire prevention and tripping hazards among the safety topics. NCSBN places safe discharge and client/caregiver education within Management of Care, so these essential elements should be addressed as part of discharge preparation rather than deferred. B is incorrect because it postpones essential equipment-use and maintenance teaching despite ATS recommending that patients and caregivers receive this training. C is incorrect because ATS includes both patients and caregivers in oxygen-safety education rather than assigning safety teaching mainly to the patient. D is incomplete and misleading because fire prevention is important, but ATS also includes equipment use, maintenance, and troubleshooting in essential patient/caregiver education; supplier involvement does not remove that training need.
educational_objective: Prepare patients and caregivers for home oxygen by teaching prescription adherence, equipment use/maintenance/troubleshooting, and fire/fall safety as part of safe discharge preparation.
source_organization: American Thoracic Society (ATS); National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_document_title: Home Oxygen Therapy for Adults with Chronic Lung Disease: An Official American Thoracic Society Clinical Practice Guideline; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
source_version_date: Official ATS guideline published 2020 (AJRCCM 2020;202:e121-e141; erratum 2021) and still listed by ATS under current Oxygen Therapy clinical practice guidelines when rechecked 2026-08-20; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective April 2026
source_locator: ATS current guideline listing, Oxygen Therapy section: 'Home Oxygen Therapy for Adults with Chronic Lung Disease: An Official ATS Clinical Practice Guideline (2020).' ATS implementation-tools page identifies Jacobs et al., AJRCCM 2020/2021 publication and erratum. Full official guideline, Education and Safety Considerations / ATS Recommendation: patients prescribed home oxygen and their caregivers should receive instruction/training on adherence to the oxygen prescription; use, maintenance and troubleshooting of all oxygen equipment; and oxygen safety including smoking cessation, fire prevention and tripping hazards; classified as a best-practice statement. NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan Management of Care: safely discharge clients, provide/coordinate client education, identify caregiver/resource needs, and collaborate with the multidisciplinary team.
source_claim_supported: The current ATS guideline listing and official guideline text directly support patient-and-caregiver education on oxygen prescription adherence, equipment use/maintenance/troubleshooting, and fire/tripping safety. NCSBN supports integrating that education into safe discharge planning.
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: safely discharge clients; provide and reinforce client education; collaborate with multidisciplinary team members; identify caregiver/support needs; and utilize resources to promote quality client care.

correction_summary: Original Q1921 contained an absolute-word distractor and distractors that omitted obvious elements of home-oxygen education. The item was rebuilt as a discharge-teaching decision in which every distractor contains a plausible partial teaching action but omits or misallocates a required ATS education component. Option lengths were balanced and the correct response now requires integrating client/caregiver teaching, equipment management, and safety. Independent post-fetch reread found no unresolved source, clinical, discharge-timing, ambiguity, cueing, blueprint, or second-answer conflict.

option_audit.A: Correct; incorporates the ATS best-practice elements of patient/caregiver instruction, prescription adherence, equipment use/maintenance/troubleshooting, and oxygen safety.
option_audit.B: Plausible partial teaching plan; incorrect because it defers essential equipment-use/maintenance education until after discharge rather than incorporating it into safe preparation.
option_audit.C: Plausible caregiver-focused plan; incorrect because ATS includes both patient and caregiver in safety education rather than concentrating safety teaching mainly on the patient.
option_audit.D: Plausible safety-focused plan; incorrect because equipment maintenance/troubleshooting education is also required and cannot simply be removed from patient/caregiver teaching because a supplier is involved.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on only/all/always/never/must-type absolute wording.
cueing_audit.answer_length: Final option lengths: A 169, B 162, C 153, D 154 characters; choices are substantially balanced and the key is not conspicuously longer.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four alternatives describe plausible discharge-teaching plans and contain clinically relevant oxygen-therapy content.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: Independent adversarial reread found no defensible second answer. B postpones required training, C omits caregiver participation in part of safety education, and D omits required equipment maintenance/troubleshooting teaching; A is uniquely complete and best.
